title: Balance & Risk — Log Walking
strapline: Wobbling along a log, balancing on stumps, judging the jump — real challenge that builds bodies, nerve and good judgement.
intent: Children develop balance, core strength and coordination through genuine physical challenge on logs, stumps and beams.
Children learn to assess and manage risk for themselves — judging what they can do and building the judgement to stay safe.
Children build confidence, courage and a can-do sense of their own capability by meeting a real challenge.
Children learn resilience: to wobble, fall, get up and try again is how the skill and the nerve are built.
Children experience the deep satisfaction and self-belief that come from mastering something that felt scary.
implementation: Offer graded challenge: a low fixed log first, then a wobblier one, stepping-stone stumps, a raised balance beam — so children choose their own level.
Risk-assess and check the equipment for genuine hazards, but allow the beneficial risk — the wobble and the height are the point, not something to remove.
Let children set their own limit — don't lift a child onto something they didn't choose to climb; readiness comes from within.
Spot without hovering: be close enough to keep them safe, far enough that they judge and balance for themselves.
Use encouraging, judgement-building language — 'where will your foot go next? do you feel steady?' — rather than 'be careful!'.
Celebrate the trying and the resilience, not just the success — 'you wobbled and you got your balance back' — so falling is part of learning.
key_questions: Where will your foot go next to stay steady?
Do you feel balanced, or a bit wobbly?
How does your body keep you from falling?
You wobbled and caught yourself — how did you do that?
Which challenge feels right for you today?

impact.text: Children balance, climb and negotiate space and obstacles with confidence and control.
Children grow in confidence, try new things and persist at physical challenges.
Children keep trying when it's hard, sticking with a wobble until they feel the win.
Children begin to assess and manage risk, judging what their body can safely do.
Children take turns and support each other on the balance challenges.

enhancements: A moveable set of logs, stumps and planks children arrange into their own balance trails.
A stepping-stone course of tree-round 'islands' at varying heights and gaps.
A slackline-style low rope or wobble board for a harder balance challenge.
Carrying a 'precious cargo' — a beanbag on a spoon — along the log for added focus.
A photo 'I did it!' wall celebrating children meeting their own balance challenges.

playing_exploring: Children explore what their bodies can do and choose their own level of challenge.
The wobble and the height invite children to test and push their own limits.
active_learning: Children persist through wobbles and falls, driven to master the balance.
Conquering a challenge that felt scary delivers pride and fuels the next attempt.
creating_thinking: Children judge risk and plan their footing, thinking ahead with their bodies.
They find their own strategies for balancing and recovering from a wobble.
